name: 2140 Prairie Avenue — the Tucker/Smith house, a red brick corner mansion banded in stone, its round corner tower, polygonal tower and square tower under crested slate caps, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3S.B. brick dwelling (D) on the 22nd Street corner, with a round corner bay, a front porch with exterior stair and a one-storey glass room lettered GLASS'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'William F. Tucker-Byron L. Smith Residence. Built 1876'.

research_note: T-3770 (piece 1 of T-1928, the S17A package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2351) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K03 red brick body over a pale stone basement, banded in stone, under a K05 slated mansard with dormers and cresting; a round tower at the Prairie/22nd Street corner, a polygonal tower on the 22nd Street flank and a square tower on the Prairie front, each under a slated cap with a crested deck (K08; the 1904 state the district draft declared, L-k01-2140-tucker-3770); K06 sash, a K07 door and the '3SB' rear range. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size and the two Chicagology photographs (forms only). The 1904 roof state of the towers is the flat-topped, crested one the 1898 plate and the second photograph show, as the district draft declared: the spires of the first photograph and the 1928 Tribune are not dated before July 1904 (L-k01-2140-tucker-3770). The porch, the glass room, the gabled dormers' crockets and the stacks' pots are T-3771's; the rear range's fittings T-3772's; the cameras and the image gate T-1929's.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); both photographs are later than 1890. Built 1876 (the marker); its loss is not read here (T-3770).

position.symbolic_location: 2140 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2140 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body at its south wall: column 672.5, row 1659 of sheet 35 at full size (T-3770), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading. Rotation -0.679 degrees, as 2130's next door on the same sheet, turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: 13.38 m from the rear wall (column 672.5) to the Prairie front (column 744.5), and 18.59 m along the front from the 22nd Street wall (row 1659) to the north wall (row 1559), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3770) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel). The rear wall's south half stands about 0.7 m further in (column 676, rows 1640-1659) and the south-west corner is cut: not built, the body is one rectangle (L-k01-2140-tucker-3770). The draft's fit had read an 8.5 by 16.25 m block and set the rest of the outline as ranges and bays.

stories.note: The 1911 sheet prints '3S.B.' on the main body: three storeys over a basement. Both photographs show two storeys of brick walling under the cornice and the third in the slated mansard, lit by its dormers; K01 counts the walled storeys.

construction.note: The sheet colours the whole body pink (brick). Both photographs show deep red brick walls banded with pale dressed stone, on a basement of the same pale stone up to the water table: K01's brick front over a stone basement, the brick carried round every wall (face_brick all_round).

stone_front.note: The second photograph's pale basement stone rises to a moulded water table at about 1.8 m over the yard (laid on the principal floor's line, 1.65 m, where K01 starts a brick front's brick) (on the round tower, the nearest wall, at about 86 px a metre: y 1290-1440 px), and pale stone bands cross the brick at the second floor (y 895-940 px, about 5.9-6.25 m) and at the second storey's springing (about 8.65 m). The stone's quarry is not read: the pale local Lemont limestone the avenue's 1870s houses were faced and trimmed with, as the photographs' tone.

face_brick.note: Both photographs show the same deep red brick on the Prairie front, the 22nd Street flank and every tower.

principal_floor_m.note: The second photograph's principal lights stand on sills about 2.0 m over the yard on the round tower (y 1275 px against the base at about y 1445 px, about 86 px a metre at the drum), so the floor about 1.65 m up (K07's stair solves its nine risers there); the 1898 plate's porch floor agrees.

storey_heights_m.note: Read off the second photograph on the round tower, the nearest wall: the second floor's stone band at about 5.9-6.25 m and the cornice's bed at about 9.8 m, its corona at about 10.5 m, so a wall head at about 10.4 m: storeys of 4.4 and 4.4 m over the 1.65 m principal floor. A camera on the pictures (T-1929) holds them.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front on its stone basement, as every K01 brick house.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

street_front_trim.note: Every light in both photographs stands under a pale stone hood over its head: K09's corniced lintel hood in both storeys, the nearest the kit lays to the photographs' arched hoods (their carving is T-1929's).

wall_head.note: A deep stone cornice on close-set blocks runs round the Prairie front, the 22nd Street flank and every tower in both photographs; it is carried round the north flank and the rear as the mansard over them is.

roof_form.note: The sheet's dashed line about 1 m inside the main body's whole outline is the key's mansard roof; both photographs show the slated mansard with its dormers over the cornice and iron cresting round its deck.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall: no picture looks down on it.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's reach in the second photograph, about half a metre past the brick.

mansard.note: The mansard's lower faces rise about 3.8 m at about 75 degrees in both photographs (the second's curb at about y 345 px over the cornice at about y 610 px between the towers). Its dormers are read where both pictures put them: one over the Prairie front's light column north of the entrance (8.7 m), one over its north bay (17.2 m) and one over the 22nd Street flank's light column (7.2 m from the rear), each under a steep gable. T-3771: the gables as both photographs draw them (the second's street dormer x 1080-1200 px, y 230-520 px): pitched steeply, about 60 degrees, a stone coping up each rake with crockets along its back, a square pinnacle engaged at each edge of the face, and a cross-topped finial at the apex (built as K01's turned finial). Iron cresting round the deck in the second photograph.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the lower faces in both photographs (the first's slates laid in bands); the deck is not seen: K05's painted tin.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: T-3771: the landing under the porch, as deep as the porch stands out (about 2.0 m in the second photograph); the flight falls from its front edge to the walk.

stoop_width_m.note: T-3771: the stair as wide as the porch it climbs to, between the porch's plinths in the second photograph, so the paired columns stand on its landing (K01: a porch's columns stand on the stoop's landing).

entrance_bay.note: The door stands in the Prairie front's second bay (5.8 m from the south wall), behind the porch the second photograph draws there and the one-storey glass room the 1911 sheet draws before it (rows 1622-1634, v 4.65-6.9).

front_bays.note: Bay centres along the Prairie front from its south wall: the light column between the round tower and the porch (both photographs), the door's bay behind the porch (the sheet's glass room), the column north of it under a dormer, and the narrow stretch north of the square tower (the sheet: v 15.8 to the north wall), whose lights no picture shows. The square tower's own lights are on its face (bays).

side_bays.note: The 22nd Street flank (K01's 'south' wall, metres from the rear): between the polygonal tower and the round one both photographs show one column of lights under a dormer, and the tall stack beside the round tower.

north_bays.note: The north flank (metres from the front) faces 2130 across a 2.9 m side yard and is hidden in every picture: three lights a storey at the kit's spacing, clear of the square tower's return.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall beside the rear wing (K01 counts it from the south): one light a storey either side of it; no picture shows it.

sash_by_storey.note: Read off the second photograph on the round tower: the principal lights about 0.95 m wide and 3.0-3.2 m tall (y 1010-1275 px), the chamber lights about 2.4 m (y 680-890 px), each on a sill a little over its floor.

basement_lights.note: Square-headed basement lights in the pale stone under the principal lights in the second photograph (y 1350-1430 px on the tower).

entrance_kit.note: T-3771: the columned porch before the door bay in the second photograph (x 1000-1290 px, y 940-1400 px; the 1898 quarter-century plate draws the same porch square-on): a stone porch about 3.0 m wide and 2.0 m out, carried at each front corner on a pair of turned shafts with carved Corinthian bells (two tiers of leaves under a thin abacus) on one plinth, a plain entablature over them (its soffit about 4.9 m over the walk, the stone frieze about 0.5 m deep under a 0.2 m cornice), and a stone balustrade about 0.6 m high round its flat top, the balcony before the door bay's chamber light. The pair stands side by side along the front, read so off the oblique; neither picture is square to the porch's flank, so a pair standing one behind the other is the alternative reading. Its straight stair falls to the walk toward the street between iron rails (the second photograph's rails, x 1050-1462 px, y 1270-1460 px), the street line 4.8 m before the front (the 1911 sheet: column 770). The first photograph's arched glass canopy over the same door, and the 1911 sheet's one-storey GLASS room there, are the later state that came with the conical spires; the declared 1904 state keeps the flat-topped towers and this porch (L-k01-2140-tucker-3771).

chimneys.note: The tall stack with its clustered pots beside the round tower over the 22nd Street flank in both photographs (the first's x 600-700 px, its pots to about y 230): stood on the deck just inside the curb, where K01 lets a stack stand (the photographs' rises from the wall), about 2.6 m over it; a second on the north side, reconstructed (the first photograph's stack behind the roof). T-3771: the tall stack's head as both photographs draw it — a row of four tall ribbed pots running back along the 22nd Street flank (four in the first photograph, x 625-700 px, y 230-330 px; three in the second, x 565-655 px, the fourth behind them), on a corbelled stone head with a dentil course and no bands down the shaft, and two narrow sunk panels down each face (the second photograph, x 580-640 px, y 350-600 px); its plan widened to 1.5 m along the flank to carry the four. The north stack, which no picture shows, stays a plain shaft with no pots or panels (reconstructed).

rainwater.note: K04's copper gutter and pipes at the back corners; no picture shows them.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the round tower's tall principal light toward the corner in both photographs (the second's x 890-970 px, y 1010-1275 px; the first's x 730-790 px), the drum blank either side of it
the round tower's chamber light over it in both photographs (the second's x 890-970 px, y 680-890 px)
the polygonal tower's tall principal lights on its three outer faces in both photographs (the second's x 120-170 and 240-300 px, y 1050-1280 px), as tall as the round tower's

the polygonal tower's chamber lights: on its three outer faces in both photographs (the second's x 120-170 and 240-300 px, y 740-930 px), and on its two returns, which the first photograph shows lit toward the corner (x 320-345 px) and no picture shows toward the rear (reconstructed alike)
the polygonal tower's stage over the main cornice, its lights in the gabled faces both photographs draw (the second's x 120-170 and 245-300 px, y 450-580 px; the first's x 420-470 px, y 495-575 px)
the square tower's paired principal lights in both photographs (the second's x 1355-1415 px)
the square tower's paired chamber lights in both photographs; its walls stop on its crown's soffit

bays.note: Three towers, as the sheet draws their plans and both photographs their forms. THE ROUND TOWER at the Prairie/22nd Street corner: the sheet's circle about 2.3 m in radius stands out of both walls (centre column 741, row 1667: about 0.65 m behind the front's plane and 1.3 m out of the 22nd Street wall). K08 builds a round tower on one wall, its ring clear of the wall's end, so it stands on the 22nd Street wall 1.3 m out with its centre 10.78 m from the rear, its ring stopping 0.3 m short of the front's plane: about 1.95 m west of the sheet's. Its drum's cornice is the main cornice in both pictures (cap_at_eave), one tall light a storey toward the corner, and its slated cap rises steeply about 3 m to a ledge and a low top (the second photograph's crested deck, which K08 does not crest on a cone). THE POLYGONAL TOWER on the 22nd Street flank near the rear (the sheet's canted projection, columns 680-698, about 3.2 m out): K08's octagon, its third stage over the main cornice lit in every face as both pictures show it under its gables, under a short slated cap and a crested deck (the second photograph). THE SQUARE TOWER on the Prairie front's north part (the sheet's projection rows 1574-1599, about 1.2 m proud and 4.65 m wide): a K08 projection with paired lights in both storeys, under its own mansard crown standing a little over the main curb with its own cresting (the second photograph). The 1904 state of all three caps is the flat-topped, crested one (the 1898 plate and the second photograph): see L-k01-2140-tucker-3770.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's '3SB' brick range behind the main body's north half (columns 644-672.5, rows 1586-1622): 5.3 m deep and 6.7 m wide, three storeys under a flat roof as the sheet's storey count and the main body's floors give; its lights and fittings are T-3772's.

boundary.note: The lot runs from the 22nd Street line (row about 1700) to 2130's lot line (row 1534); the long iron fence on the corner both photographs draw is T-1945's.

yard.note: K14's yard: a flagged walk to the stoop; the yard's planting is T-1945's.
